races.paceDynamic: Hey Havana is the sole front runner in this 14-horse field and will dictate proceedings from the start, setting a steady rhythm without pressure from fellow pace-setters. With all other 13 runners adopting hold-up tactics, the race will develop into a cavalry charge finish as the field closes on Hey Havana from the 2-furlong pole onwards. This creates a tactical nightmare for jockeys positioning themselves in the pack, with traffic problems inevitable in the final 200 yards. The lack of early pace and bunched finish clearly favours horses with tactical speed who can find a clean passage late - those able to quicken from mid-division rather than those relying on sustained finishing kicks from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Traffic Jam Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field stays bunched turning in and multiple horses get hampered in running
scenarios.body: Severe traffic problems develop as 13 hold-up horses converge on Hey Havana simultaneously. Those with good positions on the outside or who get early splits benefit most from others' misfortune.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana maintains her lead and the finish lacks the pace to peg her back
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace-pressure allows Hey Havana to control the race completely and kick again when challenged. Hold-up horses struggle to make up the ground despite their superior ratings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Clean Split Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the field splits into two groups providing racing room down the centre or far side
scenarios.body: A clear passage opens up allowing the better-rated hold-up horses to demonstrate their class advantage. Those best positioned when the gap appears can fully utilise their finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jockeys commit early to prevent Hey Havana stealing the race uncontested
scenarios.body: The race becomes genuinely run with several horses going forward from the 4-furlong pole. This sets up the patient hold-up horses with the strongest finishing kicks.

watchPoints.text: Hey Havana's early fractions will determine everything - if she goes too slow early, she becomes virtually unbeatable as the hold-up horses won't have time to close
Watch for traffic problems from the 2-furlong pole as 13 hold-up horses converge simultaneously on the leader creating inevitable trouble
Thestral and Inferno both have top jockeys who excel in these tactical scenarios and will be looking for the cleanest passages
The draw positions and how jockeys position early will be crucial with such a large field of hold-up horses needing racing room
Supreme Dancer drops significantly in class from recent efforts and could be well-treated at the foot of the weights

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Ralph will take this race by the scruff of the neck from the gates, with Flying Fletcher the only other prominent runner likely to track him early. The majority of this field are hold-up performers (Garden Oasis, Rajapour, Great Blasket, Popeye Doyle, Sunny Orange) who will settle towards the back and look to come with late runs. With only one confirmed front runner and minimal early pressure, Roaring Ralph can dictate at a steady tempo before the hold-up brigade mount their challenges in the final two furlongs. This race shape clearly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably affect the large pack of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roaring Ralph Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph gets an uncontested lead and maintains his recent winning form
scenarios.body: He can dictate terms at a comfortable pace before finding extra when the challengers come, having avoided the scramble behind. His excellent recent record (four wins from last five starts) suggests he's peaking at the right time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses get bunched up and struggle for racing room in the straight
scenarios.body: The crowded nature of five hold-up performers creates inevitable traffic problems, allowing the early leaders to steal a march. Garden Oasis and Rajapour have the class to overcome trouble but others will struggle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Garden Oasis Class Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis gets a clear run and his 11-year experience helps him navigate through traffic
scenarios.body: His proven ability on good going (three wins from six starts) and partnership with an in-form yard could see him time his challenge perfectly. Age brings racecraft that younger horses lack in these situations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph stops quickly after his recent busy spell and Flying Fletcher also fades
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between the hold-up horses, with Great Blasket's recent third at this track giving him local knowledge. However, this scenario requires both prominent runners to fail simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Roaring Ralph must break cleanly to establish his front-running position, as any early delay could see Flying Fletcher take over the lead and disrupt his tactics
Garden Oasis and Rajapour need to secure clear passages in the straight as five hold-up horses will create significant traffic problems in the final two furlongs
Flying Fletcher's ability to track Roaring Ralph without applying early pressure will determine whether the pace stays honest or becomes stop-start
Great Blasket's 7lb apprentice allowance brings him down to effective 130lbs, making him well-handicapped if he can overcome the pace bias
Sunny Orange at bottom weight could be dangerous if the hold-up horses manage to organize themselves despite the tactical disadvantage

races.paceDynamic: Newyorkstateofmind stands alone as the only confirmed front runner in this field of nine, giving him a clear tactical advantage to dictate terms from the front. With eight hold-up horses behind him, he faces no early pressure and can set a comfortable tempo over this 5½f trip. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a sustained gallop rather than a sprint finish, with the field bunched coming off the turn. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the hold-up brigade will face a wall of horses in the straight when the real running begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Newyorkstateofmind gets soft sectionals and maintains his kick
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter controls every call and has enough left to resist late challenges. Eight hold-up horses leave their move too late against a horse who has saved energy throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Swarm Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong despite no early pressure
scenarios.body: Multiple closers get first run on a tiring leader and superior class tells. The higher-rated hold-up horses find racing room and overwhelm the front runner with sustained finishing speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Newyorkstateofmind gets headed but races prominently throughout
scenarios.body: Horses able to race closer to the pace benefit from the perfect position as pure hold-up horses struggle for room. Desert Master's recent form and ability to track the leader gives him the winning edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders underperform and pace dynamics favor an outsider
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace suits a horse returning from a break or one whose style perfectly matches the race flow. Pinpoint's 142-day absence could mean peak fitness for a surprise strike.

Note any market moves for Pinpoint given long absence but trainer France rarely runs them unfit

races.paceDynamic: With all nine runners holding up tactics, there's no natural front runner to set a solid pace in this 5½f handicap. Golden Prosperity and Happier are most likely to drift forward early, but neither is a confirmed pace-setter, creating a slow early gallop. The field will bunch together through halfway before exploding into a frantic sprint finish from the 2f pole. This race shape strongly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot and proven finishing kick over those needing a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity and Happier drift forward but fail to commit to a strong gallop
scenarios.body: The field crawls through the early stages before a devastating sprint unfolds, suiting horses with the best finishing speed. Crafty Spirit and Happier possess the sharpest turn of foot to capitalize on the tactical affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses forces the issue earlier than expected
scenarios.body: A more honest pace develops when someone breaks ranks at halfway, creating a more even test. This suits the most consistent performers who can quicken off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes exceptionally slow with the field still bunched at the furlong pole
scenarios.body: An unsustainable crawl leads to a lottery finish where positioning and traffic become crucial. The best drawn and most experienced campaigners gain the edge in the melee.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Breakaway Attempt
scenarios.trigger: If Solar Biricz or another runner makes an early move to avoid the sprint finish
scenarios.body: A surprise front-running move changes the complexion but likely fails over this minimum trip. The field reels in the leader for a conventional finish favoring the holdouts.

races.paceDynamic: With all 10 runners showing hold-up tendencies and no confirmed front runner, this race will drift into a crawling early pace with minimal pressure through the first mile. The field will bunch up approaching the final two furlongs, creating a cavalry charge finish where positioning and a clear run become crucial. Horses like Bradbury and Heart Sign with recent winning form will need to overcome traffic problems, while those drawn well or with tactical pace can steal a march. This setup heavily favours hold-up horses with a turn of foot who can find gaps in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes the initiative early and they crawl through halfway
scenarios.body: The field will bunch dangerously entering the straight, creating a messy sprint where horses with recent winning form and tactical speed can exploit gaps. Those who get first run or find the cleanest passage will prevail in a photo finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners drift forward to avoid the kickback despite their hold-up style
scenarios.body: A steadier rhythm suits the more exposed handicappers who need every yard of the trip to wind up their finishing kicks. The race becomes more of a test of stamina over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field stays bunched turning for home and multiple horses get blocked
scenarios.body: Several fancied runners will meet trouble in running, allowing an outsider with a clear passage to sneak through on the rails or widest of all. This becomes a lottery based purely on racing luck.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Breakaway Holds
scenarios.trigger: If a horse like Mohaasset or Give Me Sun goes forward early despite their usual hold-up style
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time in front and has enough left to resist the late charge from horses giving away lengths at the start. The hold-up horses find the gap too big to bridge.

Monitor the early pace as no confirmed leader could create an unsustainably slow gallop that turns into a lottery
Keep an eye on Bradbury's ability to handle top weight in a sprint finish after recent winning form
Watch for Clear Above and Give Me Sun potentially going more forward than usual to avoid the inevitable traffic
Observe if the returning runners Rugby Union and Here Comes Louie show any ring-rustiness after long layoffs
